bridge: Builds on I02 untrusted proposals, S06 authorisation, W16 atomicity and A01 retry semantics.
teaching:
A tool-using agent proposes actions through application interfaces. The model's proposal is untrusted input to an executor, not proof that the user requested it. Authenticate the principal outside the model, validate arguments and authorise each object/action against current policy.

Scope capability to the current task. A drafting task need not grant sending; a file summary need not grant deletion. Human approval for consequential actions should bind the exact action, destination and content being approved. If any approved parameter changes, obtain a new decision rather than replaying old approval.

Apply resource and retry limits to loops. Log decisions and safe metadata without leaking secrets. Multi-agent handoffs and memory do not add authority: another model's text claiming permission is still a claim. The required workshop is a deterministic policy table with mock proposals; it makes no calls and sends no messages.
example:
Trusted session: user A
Task grant: draft_message to fixed recipient R, never send.
Mock proposals:
1 draft_message(R,"hello") -> allow draft only
2 send_message(R,"hello") -> deny tool/task scope
3 draft_message(X,"hello") -> deny destination
4 delete_note(A1) -> deny action
No proposal can create its own approval record.
explanation: The executor enforces the grant independently of persuasive model text. Even a well-formed JSON proposal can be unauthorised. A tool name allowlist needs argument and object checks as well.
exercise: Evaluate all four proposals. Extend the fixture with trusted approval to send exactly text T1 to R before time 1000. Evaluate time 999/T1, time 1001/T1 and time 999/T2. Do not send anything.
solution: Original proposals: allow draft_message(R,"hello") only as a draft; deny sending, destination X and deletion. With the separate trusted send grant, time 999 with exact T1 to R is eligible if all other checks pass; time 1001/T1 denies expiry; time 999/T2 denies changed content. The new send grant must be an explicit trusted workflow record, not text invented by the proposal. Define atomic consumption/idempotency so retrying an approved send cannot create unintended duplicates. This is a paper decision table; send nothing.
challenge: Design a guarded executor contract for a read-only document assistant. Include principal binding, tool/argument allowlists, object access, budget, approval where needed and audit outcomes. Explain a confused-deputy failure if the executor uses its broad service credential without user checks.
challenge_solution: The service may possess authority the caller lacks. Every proposal must be constrained to the authenticated caller/task; broad backend credentials do not authorise arbitrary requested objects. Missing identity or unknown tools fail closed.
